title: When the Compass Breaks
premise: Felix Eriksen, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Meridian Syndicate, is hired by his old rival Ines Varga for a salvage run to the Sunda Archipelago — a job his late father swore off after a disaster that killed Felix's mother. The prize is a sunken survey vessel holding his family's stolen inheritance: patents and charts worth enough to erase every debt. But the monsoon arrives early, the boat begins to fail, and the crew must accept help from Amara, a stranger with her own claim on the wreck. As storms close in, Felix discovers Ines orchestrated everything to force a reckoning with the past, and he must choose between reclaiming his inheritance and saving the people who have become his true belonging. In the end, Felix surrenders the fortune to buy his crew's freedom, keeps only his father's broken compass, and finds that what he inherited was never money at all.
about_author: Paloma Ravensworth is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck salvage claims before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels from a converted trawler moored off the Cornish coast, where she insists the weather improves her prose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Felix Eriksen's POV. A storm chase goes wrong in the Gulf of Tonkin, and Felix returns to port to find the Meridian Syndicate's collectors waiting. The emotional beat is claustrophobic dread masked by bravado as he realizes his debts have outgrown his courage.

chapters.title: A Name He Swore Never to Say
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ines Varga appears at the dockside bar with an offer: one salvage job, triple pay, debt erased. Felix refuses, remembering the vow his dying father extracted from him. The beat is bitter nostalgia curdling into anger.

chapters.title: The Crew Votes With Their Stomachs
chapters.summary: Tomas, the engineer's POV. Hungry and unpaid, the crew quietly votes to take Ines's job behind Felix's back. Tomas delivers the news, and Felix's authority cracks. The beat is loyalty tested by poverty.

chapters.title: Terms Written in Salt Water
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix negotiates with Ines aboard her gleaming yacht, learning only fragments: a wreck called the Halcyon Star, coordinates sealed, monsoon season approaching. The beat is uneasy alliance, two rivals shaking hands over old wounds.

chapters.title: What Papa Buried at Sea
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in young Felix's POV. His father burns charts on the beach after the disaster that killed Felix's mother, swearing the family will never return to the archipelago. The beat is grief as inheritance.

chapters.title: Departure at Slack Tide
chapters.summary: Amara's POV, introduced obliquely. From a fishing skiff, a woman watches the crew's boat, the Kestrel, leave harbor, checking a photograph against the faces on deck. The beat is quiet, patient menace — or is it hope?

chapters.title: Charts That Lie Politely
chapters.summary: Navigator Priya's POV. Priya discovers Ines's supplied charts contain deliberate errors near the target zone and confronts Felix privately. The beat is dawning suspicion: they are being steered, not hired.

chapters.title: The First Squall
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A sudden squall tests the crew and reveals hairline fractures in the Kestrel's hull. Felix earns back a measure of respect handling it. The beat is competence as redemption, briefly.

chapters.title: Ines at the Rail
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Alone at night, Ines reviews her own hidden agenda — she needs Felix specifically because his father hid something aboard the Halcyon Star no salvage sonar can find. The beat is ambition braided with guilt.

chapters.title: The Stranger Overboard
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. During a supply stop, they catch Amara stowing away; she claims to be a marine archaeologist with knowledge of the wreck site. Felix wants her thrown off; the crew outvotes him again. The beat is friction sparking curiosity.

chapters.title: Amara's Bargain
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara offers exact coordinates in exchange for passage and a share, revealing she lost family to the same disaster that haunts Felix. The beat is two griefs recognizing each other across a chart table.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors Don't Wait for Weather
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A Syndicate gunboat shadows them, radioing deadlines: deliver or default. Felix realizes Ines may have sold their route. The beat is paranoia tightening like a winch.

chapters.title: The Hull Sings
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Below decks, Tomas finds the hull damage worsening faster than possible and suspects sabotage — someone aboard? The beat is creeping dread inside the crew's own home.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Satellite data shows the monsoon arriving weeks early; they have a narrow window to reach the wreck and get out. The beat is the clock starting to audibly tick.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Wheel
chapters.summary: Felix and Ines share a night watch. Ines admits she knew Felix's mother, hints the disaster wasn't pure accident, and stops short of the whole truth. The beat is intimacy built on withheld things.

chapters.title: The Sabotage Revealed
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara catches the Syndicate's embedded agent tampering with the bilge pumps; a violent struggle leaves the agent overboard and Amara injured. The beat is trust earned in blood.

chapters.title: Patching a Dying Boat
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The crew improvises hull repairs with sailcloth and epoxy while the sea grows uglier. Felix works beside them, finally one of them rather than above them. The beat is camaraderie forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Coordinates of the Damned
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They arrive at the wreck site — directly over the reef where his mother died. Felix freezes at the helm; Amara gently takes his hands off the wheel. The beat is the past surfacing like a corpse.

chapters.title: Descent Into the Green Dark
chapters.summary: Felix and Amara dive the Halcyon Star. Inside, Felix finds his father's hidden strongbox — and evidence his father sabotaged the ship himself to keep the inheritance from the Syndicate. The beat is shattering disillusionment.

chapters.title: What the Strongbox Holds
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Surfacing, they open the box: patents, deeds, and a letter naming Amara's family as partners betrayed by Felix's father. The inheritance was stolen twice. The beat is moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Gunboat Returns
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Syndicate vessel arrives with the storm's first edge, demanding the box. Ines unexpectedly stalls them, buying hours — her motives still unreadable. The beat is enemies becoming temporary allies.

chapters.title: Running Before the Wind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A desperate escape run through rising seas, the patched hull groaning. Priya navigates channels no chart shows, guided by instinct. The beat is exhilaration threaded with terror.

chapters.title: Leaking Into the Storm
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The temporary patch fails; the Kestrel takes water fast as the monsoon hits full force. They must shelter or sink. The beat is helplessness against indifferent nature.

chapters.title: Haven on a Nameless Isle
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating short POVs. The crew beaches the sinking Kestrel on an uncharted island, salvaging what they can. The beat is exhausted gratitude and the strange peace of having nothing left.

chapters.title: Firelight Reckonings
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Around a driftwood fire, truths surface: Ines confesses she engineered the job to force Felix to face his father's crime, because her own brother died aboard the Halcyon Star too. The beat is grief shared at last, honestly.

chapters.title: Amara's Choice
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara holds the letter that could legally strip Felix of everything; she could take the inheritance alone. Watching the crew sleep, she chooses partnership over vengeance. The beat is forgiveness as an act of will.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Finds the Island
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At dawn, Syndicate boats ring the lagoon. The collectors offer Felix a deal: the box for the crew's lives and clean ledgers. The beat is a trap dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Forty Hours of Rain
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Trapped by weather and guns, the crew plans a desperate gambit: use the storm itself, running the Kestrel's repaired sister-sloop through a channel only Priya believes exists. The beat is hope assembled from wreckage.

chapters.title: Ines Plays Her Last Card
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines walks into the Syndicate camp offering herself and her yacht as collateral, secretly buying the crew time to prepare. The beat is sacrifice from the person Felix trusted least.

chapters.title: Launch Into the Teeth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The escape run begins — mountainous seas, the Syndicate in pursuit, the hull screaming. Felix steers not from charts but from his father's compass, which spins wildly yet somehow points true. The beat is faith over certainty.

chapters.title: The Compass Breaks
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. At the channel's worst bend, the compass shatters; Felix, blinded by spray, must steer by Amara's voice and his own memory of his mother's stories about these waters. The beat is inheriting knowledge instead of gold.

chapters.title: Through the Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The impossible channel passage succeeds; the pursuing gunboat, heavier and prouder, wrecks on the reef. The beat is cathartic triumph purchased with terror.

chapters.title: Wreckage and Survivors
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They rescue Syndicate sailors from the water, including the head collector, who now owes them his life. The power dynamic inverts entirely. The beat is mercy as the ultimate leverage.

chapters.title: Ledgers Torn in Half
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Using the rescued collector as witness, Felix negotiates: the patents go to Amara's family and a fund for all the disaster's victims; the Syndicate's claims dissolve. The beat is justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: Ines, Washed Ashore
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines survives her gamble, stripped of her yacht and fortune, oddly lighter for it. She and Felix part not as rivals but as something quieter — two people who buried the same ghosts. The beat is bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Kestrel
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Weeks later on the island, the crew rebuilds the beached Kestrel into a working boat again, Amara now permanently among them. The beat is belonging made physical, plank by plank.

chapters.title: Letters to the Dead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reads his father's full letter at last, forgiving the man who broke everything trying to protect him, and scatters the ashes of the burned charts' copies into the sea. The beat is grief finally set down.

chapters.title: A New Heading
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The crew debates their future: storm chasing for science, salvage for communities, no more debts. Felix asks Amara to navigate with him, personally as well as professionally. The beat is love arriving without announcement.

chapters.title: Storm Season, Chased Willingly
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The rebuilt Kestrel sails into open water toward a forecast storm — this time chosen, not owed. Felix carries no compass at all. The beat is freedom as a heading, not a place.

chapters.title: When the Compass Breaks
chapters.summary: Final ensemble chapter. On deck under clearing skies after the storm, each character reflects in turn: Priya at the charts, Tomas in the engine room, Amara at the bow, Felix at the wheel. The closing beat: you don't need a compass when you finally know where you belong.
